papers.title: Photografted dual-network zwitterionic hydrogel coatings for biomaterials
papers.authors: Barrera G, Wu A, Peel A, Elmer N, Hansen KR, Xu L, Hansen MR, Guymon CA.
papers.summary: A second, interpenetrating network makes the zwitterionic coating tougher and less swollen while keeping its antifouling; in rats, capsules around coated silicone were about 75 percent thinner at six weeks.

papers.title: Development of zwitterionic hydrogel thin film coatings of cochlear implant electrode arrays that reduce intracochlear inflammation and electrode impedance
papers.authors: Ben-Shlomo N, Peel A, Etler C, et al.
papers.summary: Human cochlear implant arrays with the coating read about half the electrode impedance of uncoated arrays in sheep, and the cochlea showed less inflammation at four weeks.

papers.title: Enhancing Mucus Flow and Clearance by Grafting Zwitterionic Hydrogel Films to Luminal Surfaces
papers.authors: Horne R, Escudero C, Ellerman M, Guymon CA, Hansen M.
papers.summary: On the bench, mucus began to flow at a gentler tilt on coated silicone sheets and tubes, and a dried mucus plug cleared sooner in a preliminary test.

papers.title: Photografted Zwitterionic Hydrogel Coating Durability for Reduced Foreign Body Response to Cochlear Implants
papers.authors: Peel A, Bennion D, Horne R, Hansen MR, Guymon CA.
papers.summary: The coating kept its low friction after three weeks in mice, after drying and rewetting, and under repeated bending. Coated arrays needed about half the peak force to enter human cadaver cochleae.

papers.title: Reducing the foreign body response on human cochlear implants and their materials in vivo with photografted zwitterionic hydrogel coatings
papers.authors: Horne R, Ben-Shlomo N, Jensen M, et al.
papers.summary: In mice, coated silicone and coated human implant arrays had thinner scar capsules than uncoated ones, and the film was still intact after one year.

papers.title: Zwitterionic Photografted Coatings of Cochlear Implant Biomaterials Reduce Friction and Insertion Forces
papers.authors: Bennion DM, Horne R, Peel A, et al.
papers.summary: The coating cut friction on silicone by more than 90 percent and cut the peak force to insert an electrode into human cadaver cochleae by about 40 percent.

papers.title: Antifouling and Mechanical Properties of Photografted Zwitterionic Hydrogel Thin-Film Coatings Depend on the Cross-Link Density
papers.authors: Jensen MJ, Peel A, Horne R, et al.
papers.summary: The amount of cross-linker sets how stiff the film is and how well it resists protein, cells and friction. The best balance in the lab came at roughly 5 to 15 percent cross-linker.

papers.title: Photograftable Zwitterionic Coatings Prevent Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis Adhesion to PDMS Surfaces
papers.authors: Shen N, Cheng E, Whitley JW, et al.
papers.summary: Coated silicone held far fewer S. aureus and S. epidermidis in the lab. In rats it carried fewer bacteria 21 days after implantation.

papers.title: Antifouling Photograftable Zwitterionic Coatings on PDMS Substrates
papers.authors: Leigh BL, Cheng E, Xu L, Derk A, Hansen MR, Guymon CA.
papers.summary: A one-step UV process grafts a cross-linked film onto silicone that cuts protein and fibroblast adhesion in the lab and fails inside the gel before it fails at the silicone.

papers.title: Photopolymerizable Zwitterionic Polymer Patterns Control Cell Adhesion and Guide Neural Growth
papers.authors: Leigh BL, Cheng E, Xu L, Andresen C, Hansen MR, Guymon CA.
papers.summary: Coated stripes on glass kept protein and cells off, and nerve fibers grew in straight lines along 100 micrometre stripes.
